failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The rendered docs did well on the core risks for this task: the Tag Processor overview explicitly says to use WP_HTML_Processor for collecting element text, walking subtrees, and handling implied or missing closing tags; the HTML Processor next_token() section explains that virtual closers are visited for implied/end-of-input closes; the subtree text recipe tells callers to append only #text tokens; and get_modifiable_text() states that #text is decoded and should not be decoded again. The entity, empty-heading, uppercase-source, and implied-close cases all passed because the subjects followed those passages. The only near-miss is that trial 1 and trial 3 rely on closer-driven state rather than depth tracking; this is valid per the next_token() repeated-region guidance, but it depends on understanding virtual closers and get_tag()/is_tag_closer() behavior on those closers.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs describe virtual closers and closer depth rules, but do not show a compact token trace for implied end tags showing get_token_type(), get_token_name()/get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), and depth together.

doc_gaps.problem: The get_tag() example inside the HTML Processor docs instantiates WP_HTML_Tag_Processor, which can blur the distinction between inherited lexical behavior and HTML Processor structural behavior.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Use WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() in HTML Processor method examples, or label inherited examples explicitly so readers do not switch processors for structure-sensitive work.

doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short post-loop policy snippet showing both acceptable patterns: return accumulated text for best-effort read-only extraction, or reject/fallback when paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error() indicates the scan did not complete cleanly.
